paragraphs.text: V. THAT WE MUST DIE FOR THE SON OF GOD.

It would indeed have been fitting, Emperor Constantius, to discuss nothing more with you from the divine scriptures. We have found you to be a corrupter of the truth. From those deeds of yours we have recognized you as one of those who are called wise in their own eyes precisely because they keep to the path of folly. It would have been fitting, as we said, after all the many things we have already pressed upon you, to keep silent now, especially since we remember that it is written: "Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you will become like him"; and again: "Say nothing in the ears of a fool, or when he hears it he will mock your sensible words." But I have gathered that you still applaud yourself for the power of your arms and the empty dominion of your rule, because you can do violence to those whom you ought to have brought by reason to what you had decreed. So I wished, especially in this book, to make something known to your mind, defiled as it is by sacrilege: in all the things in which you think yourself great you are wretched, and the servants of God despise all the rage of your butchery. For we want you to hold it as fixed and plain that you will pass away together with your temporal, perishing, fragile, corruptible kingdom, and that unless you look to yourself while there is still opportunity, you will come to eternal punishment. Christians, however, will come to eternal rest and attain an incorruptible kingdom. Or will you try to maintain that through this heresy of yours you will lay hold of the kingdom of heaven? You and your fellow plague-bearers the Arians feared that we Christians would refute you and that, with truth itself crying out, you would one day be forced to surrender. So you rejected debate and decided to take refuge in the force of your fragile arms. As though with fragile arms you could overcome those who are to attain immortal gifts! You, an enemy of divine religion, think you can overcome the devout servants of Christ; you, the forerunner of Antichrist, think you can overcome the soldiers of God, whom the only Son of God deigned to invite to enjoy the eternal friendship of his divinity, saying: "Blessed are you when people hate you and persecute you with curses, and reproach you and say every evil thing against you. Rejoice and exult, for your reward is great in heaven; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you." You, powerless in everything, thought you could drive us from our position. You thought you could lay low those whom you see ready to be killed for the only Son of God, precisely because they have chosen not to be tormented in hell with you deniers but to attain the heavenly kingdom. Through the empty authority of your rule you had expected to overcome those who are shown by the very confession of their faith to be temples of God. For just as you Arians, by denying the Son of God, are marked out by the words of the prophets, the apostles and the holy Gospels as houses of the unclean spirit, so we who confess the Son of God show that we are temples of God. Your cruel and sacrilegious mind, heeding the suggestions of your fellow heretics, had presumed that the soldiers of God could be made to yield to your butchery. Yet we are those whom God calls his temples, saying: "For I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people." You had judged that you could conquer those whom the apostle urges to take up God and carry him in their bodies. You had indeed supposed that you could subdue them with the futile arms of your reign. But you see the truth now. Though you stood behind the curtain in your palace, you received my answer: all the servants of God trample on your trivial authority, and they are agreed in mind, will, zeal, strength and voice to preserve their salvation.

You can see how the more your perishable dominion deigns to rage against us, the weaker, more contemptible, emptier, feebler and more abject it is judged to be. As often as your hand, roused by fury and crime, has prevailed to destroy us, so often, we recall, have we grown and emerged more and more victorious. You have slaughtered a great many in Alexandria, you have mangled some throughout the world, and you have destroyed those who resisted you in various places. But all of these are martyrs, though that is the last thing you want to hear. We certainly believe that all those most blessed ones slain by your sword are in paradise. Believe me, we have resolved to be killed by you. We have seen that it is better to have God as our lover for all ages than to be punished with you, the imitator of Judas Iscariot and of the Jews. That is why, Constantius, we do not fear the gnashing of the serpent that you bring upon us, and we are ready to undergo any death. We who so far seem to have withstood your cruel hands can never regret our resolve, even if you slay us. For the death you threaten to inflict on us awaits everyone. But such blessedness as the holy martyrs have obtained no one, as we see, has attained except those who conquered death by dying for the only Son of God. You torture, kill and banish men dedicated to God, and you cannot give any reasons for your hatred, or say why you do these things. Because you are in error, you are even angry with us for holding to the true way. You could correct yourself by our wholesome admonition, but instead you pile cruel deeds on top of your errors. You try to wrest minds dedicated to God out of the disemboweled bodies of those of us who have resolved to keep faith with God to the very end of life's course. You see that this is so, and indeed it causes you the greatest pain, since you notice that you cannot turn us aside from this, the only religion. Nor can you draw us back from this course, in which we press on toward the prize of the upward calling. You cannot do it when you make yourself an open enemy. You cannot do it when you pretend to be a friend, for it is plain that he who deceived Eve is in you. You cannot do it when you compose your speech, through which you creep like a cancer, with the false and painted swelling of knowledge. In your edict, stained with all your crimes, you assert that you are the one who repeals all errors, though you are yourself the fount of all error; you claim to be the bearer of light, though you are beset by every darkness. Though you lack all understanding, most savage Emperor Constantius, you can at last see, at least in part from finding yourself despised, that we can in no way be turned from the way of truth. For we Christians know this to be the first business of faith: to be moved from our position by neither prosperity nor adversity, and not to be drawn away from the vigor of a resolve once taken. We perceive that by this one devout utterance, "I am a Christian; I do not want to be an apostate, as you are, Constantius," all guilt is shut out. By this one utterance the safeguard of salvation is granted, the bond of freedom and of honor. We see that by this confession we are given the shield of protection and a weapon against the devil, who rages against us through you. And you say: "Deny that you are Christians!" We stand firm against the peril that opposes us and do not shudder at your savagery as you torture us; we are encouraged rather than grieved. This is the work of the awareness that remembers that the only Son of God makes the presence of his divinity available to protect his own and make them victors. Hence the very punishment by which you think we are extinguished gives us life. For we believe that he for whose sake we suffer is with us, and so what you, our punisher, hoped would serve to torment us, we take up as an increase of strength. Hence we are not broken when your evils shake us, and the more variously we are harassed by unceasing cruelty, the more firmly we are strengthened. For he is with us who protected the Hebrew youths who believed in him in the fiery furnace. He makes our minds firm, he governs our understanding, he sets our hearts on fire with his divine love and encourages us to endure holy suffering. So none of us thinks of the death you threaten to inflict, but of immortality; none thinks of the temporary punishment you inflict, but of everlasting glory. For the holy scriptures make it plain that God's martyrs are consecrated by torments and crowned by the very testing of their suffering: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints"; and: "Though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality. Having been afflicted a little, they will be greatly blessed, because God tested them and found them worthy of himself. Like gold in the furnace he tried them, and like a sacrificial burnt offering he accepted them; in due time he will look upon them. They will judge nations and rule over peoples, and their Lord will reign for ever."

Those who, relying on the greatness of God, confidently expect to attain such happiness must therefore exult, and as they think of the joys to come, they must trample on the present evils you inflict. The divine voice of the only Son of God says: "Whoever loves his life in this world will lose it, and whoever hates his life for my sake will keep it for eternal life." We Christians cling to this divine precept. Your hook, Constantius, may rebound off our limbs and return again and again to the wounds, yet we stand and shall stand unmoved, stronger than you our torturer and all your punishments. We turn over in our minds only this: that this butchery of your cruelty is profitable to us for eternal glory. Barbarians often spare the conquered; there is room for clemency even amid arms, and certainly among those who live in savage fashion. But what you do against us is beyond words. We wish you well, we long for it to come to you, and we never cease beseeching God unceasingly for it. Yet you plunder, you proscribe, you slaughter with the sword, you punish in various ways, and you do not even allow the bodies you have ordered mangled to be buried. You forbid alms to be given. You have filled all the mines, and all the places thought fit to be called places of exile, with the great number of us who resist your cunning. You do not cease to banish the innocent and to harass them with hunger, thirst and nakedness. These evils you heap on us who long to attain eternal blessedness. And yet, most cruel emperor, whatever your savagery has inflicted on us and will still impose, observe that it is a lie. For the death you inflicted on the holy martyrs who went before us is neither death nor loss nor damage, but an investment of faith that earns interest. We Christians are always tortured by you tyrants in persecution, through a perverse kind of interrogation. For by the same means that force the guilty to confess, we are compelled to deny Christ, the only and truest Son of God. But as they are condemned as they deserve once they confess, so we are crowned because we do not deny the Son of God. For us the condemnation you inflict is victory. You remove us from your midst because in our presence you would not dare to blaspheme. For by a single word of a soldier of Christ he is laid low who dwells in you and speaks against our devout confession. He thirsts for our blood through you; he has besieged your mind. He trembles at the presence of the worshipers of God and cannot bear it when we dissent from you, who say that the Son of God is from nothing, and when we stand against your threats and, aided and protected by God's power, trample on all the cruelty of your butchery. Surely you feel yourself rebuked by the steadfastness and endurance of the servants of him who says: "Do not fear the one who can kill the body; rather fear him who can destroy both body and soul in hell." We are also encouraged to trample on you, the tyrant of all tyrants, by the exhortations of Paul, his most blessed apostle: "We are children of God; and if children of God, then heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, provided we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him"; and again: "I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory to come that will be revealed in us." Thinking of the glory of that splendor, we servants of Christ must endure all the afflictions and persecutions that the devil brings, not only through you but also through all his men. For although they are many, we are delivered from them all. We believe that the Son of God is a true Son, and while we remember that the Father and the Son are two persons, we nevertheless claim one divinity for the Father and his only Son. When he who has besieged your mind hears these just and unanswerable pleas of ours, he cannot bear the truth, and so he goads your bestial spirit to harass us as fiercely as possible and to torture us with refined kinds of punishment, because we refuse to abandon the way of salvation. That is why your excessive cruelty makes sport of our bodies: because we value faith highly and do not deny that we are worshipers of God. You bear down on us with all the forces of your butchery, thinking you will harm us. You do not know that we rejoice in the occasions of our testing, for we reckon it our greatest happiness if in this contest of righteousness it falls to us to have our throats cut for the Son of God by your executioner's hand. With devout minds we stand firm against your madness. In us he for whom we suffer conquers whatever you keep tossing about concerning us, profane man, to the injury of the divine majesty itself, with empty speech, vain talk and depraved will. All this your hard mind and the obstinate savagery of your heart bring forth to the death of your own salvation. You dissent from the religion of God, led by madness and swept along by fury, harried in short by all the savagery that both goads you and carries you away. Meanwhile we, protected by him whom you deny, resist your savagery, you beast, as breakwaters set against a hostile sea resist it. Let the devil's waves strike at us through you, and let the far-ranging whirlwinds of the world batter us: our strength, unmoved as it is, will become ever more unmoved. We will not be engulfed or yield beneath the waves of your attacks foaming all around us, but will always stand upright against every danger. For the Christian soul is not so abject as to be laid low and tossed into vice; it is so generous and noble that it remains unmoved and victorious against every temptation. We are not Christians who think of enjoying the sweetness of this present fragile life. We long to attain the glory of eternal security and happiness, the possession of everlasting blessedness. The devout voice of the blessed apostle John urges us to scorn earthly things and long to pursue heavenly ones: "The world passes away, and its desire with it; but whoever does the will of God abides for ever, just as God also abides for ever."

Since this is so, I want you to know that you, with all your tricks and frauds and the vast cruelty of your savagery, lie beneath the feet of God's servants. We count all the glory of your vain dominion as nothing and hold it as nothing, and with all the force and authority of your empire you are regarded by us as nothing but an empty puff of air. Perhaps one of your flatterers will say that we are boasting. Do you not remember, Constantius, what I said before the judges while you listened behind the drawn curtain? I said that even if you decreed that your whole army should hurl the weapons of your realm at us, and dash all their arms against us as men who curse your blasphemy and despise your sacrilegious decree, even so we could not draw back from our resolve. But you, in that wisdom of yours, judged that your soldiers should die for you in every war, while you decreed that Christians ought to become deniers of God. Your men certainly feel the pain of their wounds; they grieve that they have perished, they grieve to lose this light. But we, first of all, cannot feel the torments of punishment, for in us Christ suffers, and in us Christ works eternal salvation. Second, we count present things as nothing and shall be for ever in that everlasting light. How could it be, then, that we should not prefer to be killed by your sacrilege-defiled hands for Christ the Son of God, the giver of eternal life? We see that we cannot please God the Father in any other way. When you summon us to deny his only Son, we must confess, even through death itself, that he is the true Son of God. Your detestable mind resents our saying that Christ the Son of God is the Word of God, the Wisdom of God, the Power of God, true God from true God, born of the Father, that is, of the Father's substance, light from light, begotten not made; that he is of one substance with the Father, which the Greeks call homoousion; that through him all things were made; and that without him the Father never was. You resent it, worm of Arius, that we maintain that the Father and his only Son have one splendor, one power, one greatness, one eternity and one divinity. You resent our claim that what we envoys asserted in your palace, and do not cease to confirm, is not new. It has always been believed by Christians and is believed still, just as the holy faith is seen to have been set down at Nicaea against your Arian heresy and against all errors. If you would at last open the eyes of your heart, pierced by the serpent's bites, you would find that this is what the church holds [?]. The church defends this faith, which it knows was handed down to it through the blessed apostles. If you could travel through all nations in a moment, most stupid emperor, you would find that Christians everywhere believe as we do. You would find that they persist in this defense of ours and long, as we do, to die for the Son of God. But your novel preaching and newfangled religion is blasphemy that you have put forth under the pretext of faith, to the ruin of your own salvation. Even with all your efforts it has so far been unable to spread throughout the Roman frontier. More than that, wherever it has tried to put down roots it has withered, since all God's servants withdraw from you. Only your few remain with you, whom the Lord foretold would be tares sown over the wheat. All this has been supplied to you, and is still being supplied, by the craftsman of fraud and death. Through you he entices and deceives very many with crooked flatteries. Though he himself is guilty of every crime, he prompts that most bitter heart of yours to punish us as if we were guilty of some crime. But look ahead at last. Open the eyes of your heart, in which there is no light for you, only gloom and vast darkness. Then you will find that the death you inflict through your fragile power restores a more perfect life. You will find that it rather leads us to glory, through fires, swords, chains and wild beasts, through whatever, in short, the rage of you, our "most pious emperor," decides to heap upon us to kill us. With God protecting us, we are not only not extinguished but are made more and more alive, for we remember that there is nothing above us except God. Hence a soul devoted and given over to God is ashamed to yield to you, who are dead through your blasphemy, a dog barking against the truth, swarming with the worms of Arius. Whenever the souls of Christ's servants carefully examine the true force of torments, they conclude that there is no greater torment than for a servant of Christ to be conquered by you, the servant of our adversary. We remember that the Lord said: "If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it. For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world but suffers the loss of his own soul? Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul?" The dignity of martyrdom compels us Christians to condemn life by death. For through the Son of God a new kind of salvation has been granted: to die so as not to perish. We know that this discipline has been handed down to us from God: that we should defend without any fear the strength of the warfare that bears so great a name. Long ago the longing for eternal remembrance drew us away from desire for this light, and fellowship with Christ set us apart to trample on all earthly things. The battle of your cruelty grows, Constantius; but notice that the glory of Christ's soldiers grows too. We are not held back from the battle line by fear of torments; rather, your torments themselves call us out to battle. You will not be able to deny that this is so when you see Christians throughout the world encouraged to wage the contest with an equal and like ardor of courage. You will see the incorruptible firmness of faith of Christ's soldiers: your detestable flatteries do not deceive them, the threats of your fury do not terrify them, and the torments of your butchery and the tortures of your cruelty do not overcome them. For he remains in us and is always with us who said to the blessed apostles: "I am with you always, to the end of the age." He is present everywhere, because as the Son of the Almighty he is all-powerful, and he shares with the Father one eternity and one divine power.

No words can describe how thick the darkness of unbelief is that has besieged you, or how dense the cloud of darkness and error that has covered your heart. You pretend to be a Christian, yet you strive to remove the Christian name from among us. Meanwhile you should recognize that readers will forgive me if my modest talent has lacked the eloquence to describe you and curse you as your impiety deserves. They saw that I had given a pattern to all who fear God and supplied material to those who will take up the subject, showing them how they might cut you down, standing as you do without the roots of eternal life. Do not say that we revile you with abusive words if you hear what you deserve from men who may be rustic but are still Christians. We know that we must not curse, but must rather pray for our enemies. For though the Son of God is Lord of all things, when he was cursed he did not curse in return. Indeed, if the Lord of all things were to curse, the whole universe would surely collapse under the force of so great a majesty. To this you will no doubt say: "The Lord wanted you to be gentle, since you are his bishop, and yet you show yourself stubborn toward me." The prophets, the apostles and the whole choir of the Gospels teach that one must not kill. You, on the contrary, think it right to slay those dedicated to God. We Christians know that to please the One we worship we need the things in which we know he delights and rejoices. If, then, we must suppose that what you do can please God, we should all be murderers, sacrilegious and blasphemers. O Constantius, you see how great your madness is! That subtle old trickster, the deceiver of the innocent, has plainly set up his seat in your mind, and do you think you have not yet been exposed? Though you are a wolf, do you still [?] as a sheep? The most holy prophets call you a beast, and the most blessed apostles call you a dog and a ravening wolf, a worker of iniquity disguised as a minister of righteousness. And do you think you are a man, when you bear nothing of a man except his features and outward shape? It pains you to be called a monstrous beast with nothing of a man but his features and outward shape. Tell me, please, slayer of the innocent: can you rightly be called a Christian? Or are you not rather a madman, dull and senseless, an enemy indeed of God's religion? For in that religion dwell piety, humanity and all righteousness. In it we learn not to return evil for evil, and we are taught not to kill but to be killed for the Son of God. Seeing that your sacrilegious attempt has made your vain dominion despised, you apply tortures. But the protector of faith, the pilot of salvation, the ruler of souls, whom you urge us to deny, is always with us and always present at our contest, and he raises up those who fight for his divine name and defend it. That is why we stand stronger while the slaves and ministers of your injustice, your fellow executioners, torture us. We are given courage, so that our beaten and torn limbs prevail over your hook. For how could the blow, raging long and repeated, overcome an unconquerable faith, when every soldier of Christ knows that the one for whom he suffers is present with him and rejoices in his servants' endurance? We servants of Christ stand firm, strengthened by his majesty, with a free voice and an uncorrupted mind. We are stripped of your frail weapons, but we are clothed in the armor that the blessed apostle begged us to put on when he said: "Finally, be strengthened in the Lord and in the power of his might." And: "Put on the armor of God, so that you may stand against the devices of the devil. For your struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places. Therefore take up the armor of God, so that you may be able to resist in the evil day and, being perfect in all things, stand firm. Gird your loins with truth, put on the breastplate of righteousness, and have your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace. In all things take up the shield of faith, with which you can quench all the fiery darts of the most wicked one. Take also the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, praying at all times in the Spirit with every prayer and supplication, and keeping watch in it." Since your cruelty and your father's cannot overcome men so armed and fortified by such power, then, as has often been said, we have stood, we stand, and until you consume our bodies we shall stand. We are protected by the saving shield of Christ, clad in the breastplate of his goodness and governed by the Holy Spirit. We are immovable, growing stronger and stronger in all things, and we reject every word that would make us slaves. For we are certain and confident that none of your snares, none of your cunning, none of your quibbling and none of your frauds can draw us away from the strength of our purpose. We know that the end of sins is death, and that after it follows the life that lasts forever. We embrace the counsels of his blessed apostle and long to be found his imitators and partners. He teaches that while our outer man is corrupted, the inner man is renewed; that if the earthly house of our body is dissolved, a heavenly one is built; and that while we are in the body we are away from the Lord. With that apostle we shall not be able to render abundant praise to God in the heavenly kingdoms unless we first vanquish death and come to receive the immortal rewards.

So when you have scattered our bodies and utterly dissolved them, we take it that we will then be most fully whole. When you have inflicted death on us, we believe that we can then live all the more. Constantius, emperor for the time being and always utterly witless, how can you still presume to inflict things that destroy you but give life to us? Evil and perverse counsel stirs you up to destroy us, and you have been driven to hurry to shed the blood of the servants of God's only Son. You do not know that our blood opens heaven and our blood quenches the burning of Gehenna. Worldly ambition urges you on. The greatness of heaven urges us on, for we fear to lose eternal salvation. We know that we ought to die for God. Unless you cross over from the devil's camp to the army stationed in the camp of heaven, the fire of Tartarus will hold you forever. Just so, if we scorn your threats and tortures and choose to have our throats cut for the Son of God by you, most savage wild beast and monstrous brute, we shall be rejoicing in heaven. For "blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." He did not say, "Blessed are those who persecute." We Christians know that we were made soldiers of Christ for this purpose: to confess our commander on the battlefield you have unjustly proclaimed, and to die under arms, so that we may win the triumphs of victory. So the more you rage, the more merciful you seem to us, when you see fit to kill someone who confesses that he is a Christian. But you are judged most wicked in this: under a show of love, as though you wished to look after us, you flatter us in order to bring us down, as if it would do us good to be dislodged from our position and kept alive by you, only to be condemned by God. We know that you are afraid we may die persevering in this faith amid all the punishments your abominable mind has devised, and yet you apply various harsh tortures. You persecute us so savagely that you want us butchered in various ways at every moment, yet you have decreed that we are not to be killed. It is as if only death made the soldiers of Christ blessed, and tortures did not also produce greater glory for virtue the heavier they were. We know that the life of righteousness is richer and longer, so we do not turn our backs on this battlefield, and we do not cross over to your camp, enemy of God. Rather, placed amid the destruction you inflict, we long to be restored to God's sheepfold, from which the devil has snatched you and now possesses you. And yet I do not say this so that you will spare us. You will find that we are Christians, just as you found those you have already killed steadfast in faith, patient in pain and victorious under interrogation. They prevailed through him who does not desert his confessors. As you see, we recognize that we are his soldiers, and so we engage bravely and fight steadfastly. For we know that it is a great glory, an immense sublimity and truly a singular [?] to adorn the life of eternal salvation with the honor of suffering. We know that the greatest nobility is to despise the tortures of your power and not [?] them, and to trample on you without fearing your rage. You rage so madly against the innocent. You are a teacher of blasphemy, injustice and every cruelty, and yet you think you can appear to be a Christian, pious, prudent and just, blind and dull and ignorant of the truth as you are. Mark this, devourer of the innocent: the one in whom Christ keeps watch cannot be conquered by your tortures. He conquers hunger and scorns thirst. By the vigor of his strength he masters the squalor of prison and the horror of the penal cell. He tramples every punishment, crushes every torture, and does not fear the death that you strain so hard to threaten. Do you think you can overcome a man who remembers that it is written: "What shall I render to the Lord for all that he has rendered to me? I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord. Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints"? And: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or the sword? As it is written: For your sake we are put to death all day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter. But in all these things we overcome through him who loved us."

I cannot see at all what of yours could take us away from these saving precepts. You use the whole of your impious office without ceasing to advance those who consent to your depravity, so as to entice us. Such are Epictetus and the rest, whom you have turned from servants of God into your own men and into satellites of your father. Yet far be from us the madness of putting the false before the true, or of letting any prosperity under your reign that you might offer entice us. Keep vain glory for yourself. Keep all the prudence of your utterly stupid heart for yourself and for your peers, to whom likeness of character has joined you. Leave us our folly: when we confess that Christ, the Son of God, is the true Son; when we maintain that he is of one substance with the Father; when we declare that we would rather be killed for him than deny his divinity. Leave us folly of this kind. Why do you labor to make us lose it? Why do you think that you can assail the truth, not knowing that it prevails by its own power? How else do you see God's people resisting your fierce roaring and harsh tortures with unconquered strength, except that the faith we defend is apostolic and evangelical? These people resist your cruelty and trample on your rage. Their hope is eternal immortality and heavenly life. Their ardor is kindled into a longing for perpetual light, and their salvation rejoices in the promised blessedness. We are so secure, knowing that we shall come to enjoy eternal life, that we endure all things gladly. For we declare that we do not think of our own torments, but of the punishments that await you, the torturer. We Christians repay the losses of the body with the gains of the soul. We count a crown in our wounds, and over the tortures and pains you inflict we triumph in Christ with the greatest joy.

Remember, Constantius, the fresh memory of the crimes you branded on yourself in the city of the Alexandrians. Remember how many a single stroke of your signature hurled down precipices; how many it had cut down by the sword; how many it had wasted away by hunger and thirst or killed in prison; how many it had strangled by cutting off their breath. Yet though you raged with all these cruelties against the holy martyrs whom your gladiator's spirit killed, you rage more cruelly against us. You hold back the sword, and you take care that the release of death does not come too quickly to our relief. We endure having our whole bodies torn apart and burned. We prove that nothing so befits the gravity and constancy of the wise as to be driven from their judgment and purpose by no terrors. We prove that it is most profitable to be tortured for God; that those who belong to God cannot die and cannot be conquered by unending tortures; and that it is you, rather, who are overthrown and brought to nothing. Hear what is set down in the twenty-sixth psalm: "The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid? When the wicked draw near against me to devour my flesh, my enemies who afflict me, they themselves have grown weak and fallen. Though an army encamp against me, my heart shall not fear. Though battle rise up against me, in this I will hope. One thing I have asked of the Lord, and this I will seek: that I may dwell in the house of God all the days of my life." The virtue of righteousness is perfected in these sufferings. Because Christ suffers in us, we do not even feel the punishment, for where there is no guilt there is no penalty. How, then, did you think you could conquer those dedicated and devoted to God by the very things through which unconquered faith gives them increase of virtue? I believe, and the truth does not deceive me, that you are still bending all the strength of your butchery to tear our limbs apart and, raging long as a torturer, to plough furrows in our mangled bodies down to the blood. Yet you can never conquer God's household or overcome Christ's army. You will not subdue it by pain or bend it by agonizing punishments. We Christians refuse no tortures and no death. We cannot tremble at your tyrannical commands or at your judges' swords, because we resist you armed with the sword of God. The blessed apostle says to the Ephesians: "Finally, be strengthened in the Lord and in the power of his might. Put on the armor of God, so that you may stand against the devices of the devil. For your struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness." Through you all the demons rage for our death, but since you cannot overcome those clothed in the armor of God, we urge you at last to give yourself over to us, so that you are not tormented for all ages with those whom the apostle describes. So the children of light cannot be conquered in the darkness of your prison by the son of darkness, as though those in whom the creator of light deigns to dwell could feel darkness. Virtue must bear what mortal nature has taught must be borne. If you try to consume our limbs with fire, we shall feel that it is you rather than ourselves being burned in our bodies. For we run willingly and eagerly to death for the faith, and we take it for granted that we cannot lose life, but rather gain it, and indeed gain eternal life after this frail one. The edge of your sword stands always drawn and ready for the slaughter of Christians. Yet that blade of your sword seems to us blunter [?] than any lead, as does the edge of your soul. We endure all things, secure in our suffering, as though we were the ones inflicting the punishments we suffer, since the one who rages against us through you is laid low by our faith. We have believed in Christ, the giver of eternal life, the only true Son of God, and so we know that a death inflicted by your perpetual malice cannot destroy us. We believe and rightly assume that even the bodies you now burn, torture and tear will rise to light and everlasting life. If we knew that we would be nothing after you killed us, we would certainly be utter fools not to look after this life and make it as long as possible and full of every comfort. That could have been ours if we had decided to be governed by your decrees rather than God's. But as it is, if you take away the present life, an immortal one is received. So his servants must despise this present life and its goods for the sake of the Son of God, since every such loss is repaid with immortality.

Consider, Constantius, how great the virtue, how great the strength of mind, and how firm the faith were in those you killed, and still are in those who resist your sacrilege. Some are the blessed martyrs whom we see already established by God's power in the heavenly kingdoms. Others you have not yet been able to kill. All of them have stood firm against you, monstrous beast, who never cease to threaten us with things that can be spoken and things that cannot. You always have found, and still find, it far more bearable to hear that rival princes are rising against you than that those who confess Christ, the Son of God, have emerged victorious. Your heart, besieged by the darkness of every error, and your mind, blinded by deep gloom, had resolved to turn us all away from God through your heresy, to make us first your clients and then your fellow satellites. But the truth has conquered you, and also the one in you who undertook to contrive these schemes, for the truth prevails by its own power. So we are waiting at every moment for you to add still more to the tortures you have already inflicted. Appoint more savage executioners and fiercer avengers, who can attack with the sword, crucify, roast with fire, or tear our entrails and limbs with some unheard-of kind of punishment. Let them do it to the soldiers devoted to God who resist your deadly edicts, so that by the strength of faith, through God's mercy, we may trample on your threats, tortures and torments. As we have stood immovable through the Lord until now, so we shall always stand. It is not we who overcome your gnashing teeth, but he in us, by whose help we are guided and by whose power we are kept safe. For how great are you, or what sort of being, that you could rob us of the goods that God has bestowed on us? You plunder us, [you deny us,] you make us destitute, you condemn us, you put us in chains, you burn us, you even kill us in wretched ways. Yet you cannot conquer the unconquered faith of Christians. From this you should have understood how things are arranged. You too will receive the punishment for your error and cruelty. We, for our part, cannot yield to your cruelty, since through this hardship set before us the narrowest path leads loftily to the reward of immortality. We know that martyrdom is a singular imitation of the Lord's fortitude. The martyrs' road is indeed so full of toil and difficulty, and so steep, that no one can complete it by human strength. But we are aided by the help of divine support, and so we must always trample on you, as we trample on you now. That is why it pleases us not only to have no fear of you, the adversary of God's religion, but even to provoke you of our own accord. And you are provoked, since you are always expected, merciless as you are, not to show mercy but to kill. That is why our happiness cannot be divided. Even when we are killed for the Son of God, he himself lives in us through love: he who is encouragement in affliction and strength in the battles of persecution. Whatever ways you choose to show yourself against the worshippers of God, you will never be able to empty the virtue that has been sealed, since worldly things do not allure it and tortures do not terrify it.

Since this is so, what else can I call you, persecutor of God's house, but wretched? You obey the promptings of the demons, your robber chiefs. Driven by their goads you have plotted to commit these crimes, and through them you gladly go astray, your sacrilegious conviction clinging to your heart. Indulge, then, the folly you were born with. If only you were content to err and rave with your fellow blasphemers the Arians alone! But you try to drag us too into partnership in your evils: you proscribe us, you strip us of our goods. Yet we know that poverty sought for Christ's sake is the highest kind of happiness. You bring death upon us, executioner. We do not pull back our necks; we offer them, so that we may be slaughtered for the only Son of God. Why have I said this? So that you may know that your punishments have no power against the servants of Christ, and that we cannot dread what we are always expecting to come. You take it ill that you are called a heretic, and yet you dare to say that the Son cannot be compared or made equal to the Father. We, who defend the one deity of Father and Son, say that the Son is equal to the Father. We believe it as the blessed apostle Paul believed it, who says of the Son: "Who, being in the form of God, did not count it robbery to be equal with God." What does "being in the form of God" mean, except that the Son is, as God the Father is, unchangeable, unalterable, beyond all reckoning, beyond all telling, eternal and perfect? What does "being in the form of God" mean, except that the Son dwells in the same unapproachable light as the Father, and that the divine majesty of Father and Son is one? The Holy Spirit, abiding in the blessed apostle and already then seeing all your heretics' hearts, added an explanation of what it means for the Son to be in the form of God: "Who, being in the form of God, did not count it robbery to be equal with God." The blessed apostle says that the Son is equal to the Father, and so shows that the deity of Father and Son is one. And you dare to say, with the henchmen of your sacrilegious audacity and the partners in your sacrilege: "We cannot make the Son equal to the Father or compare him with the Father." Why then do you think the Lord said, "He who has seen me has seen the Father," and, "I and the Father are one," unless the power of Father and Son is one? You say that the Son has a beginning. We say that he is without beginning, since whatever has a beginning must also be capable of having an end. We believe that the only Son of God is eternal, that is, coeternal with the Father, and you enemies of God deny it. Are we not then entirely right to call you madmen, sons of pestilence crammed with every folly? It is of you that the blessed apostle cries out, as he did then of the Jews: "And since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do what is not fitting." To the Philippians he writes: "Brothers, join in imitating me, and observe those who walk in the way you have us as a pattern. For many walk, of whom I have often told you and now tell you even with tears, as enemies of the cross of Christ. Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame; they set their minds on earthly things." And to Timothy he writes of you, Constantius, and of your dearest companions in perdition: "But the Spirit says plainly that in the last times some will depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons, through the hypocrisy of liars whose consciences are seared." The Holy Spirit still strikes you down and slays you by the mouth of the same blessed apostle Paul: "In the last days perilous times will come. People will be lovers of themselves, covetous, proud, haughty, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, wicked, without natural affection, faithless, slanderers, without self-control, savage, without kindness, traitors, reckless, puffed up, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God, having the appearance of godliness but denying its truth. Avoid these people too." And further on: "Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these also oppose the truth, men corrupt in mind and worthless in the faith. But they will not get any further, for their folly will be plain to all, as theirs was." And further: "The time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine, but to suit their own desires they will heap up for themselves teachers who tickle their ears, and they will turn their hearing away from the truth and turn aside to fables."

You have deserted the apostolic faith and turned to fables. Your talk spreads like a cancer, just as the Holy Spirit foretold by the mouth of the apostle. You call catholics strays from the truth. A little later you call blasphemy the very faith you had called catholic and were forcing us to accept. Shortly after that, the faith you had just declared at Antioch to be blasphemy, when you were acting against Eudoxius, you now affirm once more as catholic. That is why you decided that Eudoxius should be at Constantinople: you had approved him as catholic. Learn from this, then, how great the difference is between true and false. You think yourself learned, and you keep a fixed number of secretaries to compose for you, yet we see that you have persuaded no one except those who feared your butchery. We, by contrast, have barely enough natural ability to speak, and know nothing at all of pagan literature, yet we are strong enough to destroy every heresy, because the facts themselves and the truth do the speaking. You and your helpers have enlarged the art drawn from pagan letters; we know only the sacred letters. Our speech is plain. Yours is polished and ornate, and might even deserve to be called eloquent. And yet your speech, crafted by art to persuade sweetly, can persuade no Christian except one who is not really a Christian but only called one, like you. You are a wolf, yet the ignorant take you for one of the sheep. Who is so senseless, except you, who have drunk down every kind of madness? Which of God's servants would not wish to be honored with death in the service of devotion? Who does not long to shed his blood for Christ, since such a death makes life more complete and wins eternal glory? We stand, as you see, protected by the power of God, shod with the precepts of the gospel, our step fixed and immovable, so that you cannot sweep our feet away in a headlong fall. We stand holding the shield of faith, so that the enemy's smoking darts, hurled through you, cannot take hold at all, since they always rebound on you. Our heads are guarded by the helmet of salvation, and the word of the Lord is in our mouths, so that the enemy lodged in you may be struck down by the spiritual sword, laid low and scattered. You will find that the holy faith you were forcing us to throw away is the shield of our soul, strong and impenetrable, and a close-woven breastplate that none of the devil's darts, hurled through you, can pierce. Seeing such perseverance in Christians, you say: "The Arian doctrine, once I have taken it up, must be defended." You say such things in error, but with an honorable intention. For you feel that nothing in human affairs is more excellent than religion, and that it must be defended with all one's might. You defend it with the sword. We know that religion must be defended not by killing but by dying for God and by enduring all these evils you heap upon us. When religion is defended in this way, what cruelty of yours can win? If any one of your soldiers, in this frail service of your empire, keeps faith with you, mortal with mortal, in some outstanding deed, he becomes more welcome to you and dearer. If he dies in the service of you, an empty man, he wins the highest glory for having fallen for you, his commander. How much more must we, soldiers of his clemency, keep faith with God, the eternal emperor! The duty of devotion we have taken on compels us to do this. But you are blind, because you do not believe that Christ is true God, Son of the true God, and you are plainly unhappy, because you have not escaped the darkness of eternal death; and so you wanted us too to go back to our former blindness, so that we would be seen to have lost our wisdom together with the light, and not simply but detestably. For we recognize that for you there is a single condemnation to death, because you refuse to believe, but that the evil would be double for us if we rejected our faith and chose to return to destruction. How could you presume that we could be separated from the love of God, either by your false favors, which kill while they entice, or by every kind of cruel torture? Who would spurn the great happiness offered to him, unless he were more unhappy than you, when he sees that by confessing the single phrase "I am a Christian" adversities give way, joys come forth, kingdoms are opened, and eternal dominions are prepared? You say: "Deny the Son of God, or the power of my reign will kill you." How much better to be killed by Christ's enemy than by Christ! How excellent to be slaughtered by you, the friend of Antichrist, and to be brought to life by Christ! Who would not rather be found a partner and companion of the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs and all the righteous than of Judas, whose imitator you have become? John the Baptist was punished in prison by Herod, your fellow plague. The savagery of Herod killed James. The apostle John was banished to an island. Blessed Peter was crucified. The blessed apostle Paul was put in chains, shut up in prisons, scourged, often stoned, and at last killed. But we see that all these became friends of God by enduring those things most gladly, and so we too would rather be slaughtered by your cruel hand than give way to your butchery. Why do you hate us? Why do you persecute us with such savagery? Surely because we confess that we are Christians. Those blessed men we have mentioned were also killed by your fellow tyrants for the only Son of God, because they called themselves his servants. The Holy Spirit says by the mouth of devout David, speaking for our people: "If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a foreign god, will not God search this out? For he knows the secrets of the heart. For your sake we are put to death all day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter." And you, Constantius, slave of Arian idolatry and emperor for the time being, say: "Fear the gnashing of my madness as it flares up again for your death, and become apostates with me."

You hear this, yet you do not want to heal your wounds. Instead you go on raging, driven blindly and irrationally by those who slip into your mind and goad you into fury without your knowing it. These are the spirits to whom you are known to sacrifice by denying the only Son of God. By themselves they can do us no harm, for we are protected by the greatness of God. So they persecute us through you, their henchman, because they feel that we are their bitterest enemies, and through you, their lover, they carry out their savagery as violently as they can, thinking that with you as their executioner they will violate our faith. All the sacred Scriptures teach that believing in the Son of God is the first and the consummate righteousness. That is why, when you the torturer are defeated, those demons in you are defeated too: it is not the strength of our frail bodies that gives us the victory but his clemency. He supplies the strength for us to endure unmoved amid every instrument of your butchery, so that we are not broken by the pain of wounds or the blows of torture but are lifted up instead. This is the true worship of God, in which the minds of the worshipers offer themselves to God as spotless victims. Do you think that any worshiper of God is so sluggish and dull that the heat of so great a longing will not rouse him, arm him, urge him on, spur him, and finally set him ablaze with the torches of love that set the holy prophets, apostles and martyrs ablaze? Which of us, I ask, is not driven by his spirit to be killed for Christ in your cruel hands? Whom does it not urge on to reach the glory and summit of martyrdom, not only through the tortures you now apply but through even crueler ones? For your tortures are easily overcome if their glory is set before one's eyes. No one thinks about what tears his flesh when so great a reward is given for the pain. Your torments, Constantius, are defeated by incorruptible rewards. Torture is crushed and death is subdued, for when death is inflicted, life is restored all the more. The wounds you inflict, emperor, would hurt if they did not at once make us friends of God. We are confident that we shall truly live if you punish us for the Son of God, and that we shall then lose nothing of salvation. How, then, could we give way to your empty gnashing? You thought that your force could subdue us, and can still subdue us, and I believe you still think so, in vain. How long, Constantius, will you abuse the patience of God? Rather, I urge you to drive these thoughts out of your darkened mind, and let your foolish mind take in instead the reflections that can set you on the road to the kingdom of God. Gladly lay hold of what can bring you to the banquet of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the friends of God. You, a man full of every injustice, have dared to think yourself just. You have set yourself above all the bishops appointed in the holy Church by the judgment of God. You have rejected the holy faith that the Church has always held and holds still. You have striven to preach the blasphemy uttered by the mouth of Arius, your partner in sacrilege, now through your henchmen, now by your edict, now with your own mouth crammed with unclean spirits. And yet you want to be called a perfect worshiper of God who does everything in holiness, although not one of the kings called tyrants is ever found to have been crueler, more detestable, or greater in blasphemy than you. I have already shown your imprudence that this is so in the book entitled On Apostate Kings. Now I want you to know this: unless you are converted in good time, unless you believe as we do that the only Son of God has always reigned with the Father, that the Father was never without the Son, that the kingdom of the Father and of his only Son is one, and that Father and Son possess one deity, you will perish forever. For your teacher Arius called the Son of God a creature, and you have praised his blasphemy to the skies. We urge you, we beg you, we press you to become a true lover of God, and you complain that we are wronging you. In this way you guard the empty prestige of your rank, as though it could snatch you from everlasting torments. You raise your proud head above the priests of the Lord, without heeding what is written: "Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted." The apostle says of the only Son of God, whom you persecute in us: "Who, being in the form of God, did not count it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being found in appearance as a man; he humbled himself to the point of death, even death on a cross." He always was, is, and will be in the form of the Father, for he is the true Son, unchangeable and unalterable, since he is God, the all-powerful Son of the Almighty. Yet for our salvation he deigned to humble himself, so that he might raise us up and exalt us when we lay prostrate and cast down. And it is this holy humility of his that has made you bark like a rabid dog against his divine majesty. In the sacred Scriptures you see only what was written about the humility he took on, and you pass over the passages that tell of his eternal divinity.

What is your answer to this, Constantius, you whom the bishops of your Arian doctrine keep hailing as bishop of bishops? Do you, or do you not, believe that those who die for God's only Son will possess the kingdom of heaven? If you do believe it, why do you push us to deny his eternity? Why do you not stop persecuting, and leave in peace those who believe in him? Why are you always restless against us and always hostile, showing yourself a violent persecutor and, under the name of peace, a crafty enemy? I grieve that you have brought such great evils on yourself. I mourn you, because on every side you are left without hope of eternal life. For the rest, though you not only cut us with swords but even chew us with your teeth, be sure of this: protected by God, we shall overcome your rage. And do not look down on us because you see that our bodies are frail. What matters most is that we stand strong, upright and fortified by wisdom, with adornments and defenses in our hearts and minds. How is it that we now see ourselves adorned? How is it that we feel fortified and safe? How do we know ourselves to be wise? Only because we avoid your blasphemy and gladly hand over our mortal bodies to your sword for the Son of God, knowing that, though you can kill our earthly dwelling, you cannot kill the heavenly one we possess. For we know that good and evil have been set before us precisely so that the whole force of our prudence might be spent on telling good from evil. What could be more foolish than to fear you and deny God? What could be wiser than to trample on your wicked head and so become pleasing to God? That is why you see us standing ready with all our strength in the contest of righteousness, with faith intact, with devoted courage and an uncorrupted mind, standing for the battle you have declared, fearless soldiers of the living God. We also carry the shield of faith bravely, and so, with God protecting us, whatever the devil hurls by your hands is put out, because our feet are shod with the teaching of the gospel and armed with spurs. Though you are Augustus, the serpent in you that roars for the death of us innocents is crushed, since it cannot manage to bite us or trip us up through you, its executioner. God does indeed will that we be pressed hard by you, but certainly not so that we may abandon the faith and the path of the patriarchs, apostles and martyrs. Rather, he wills that, when you try to force us to deny God's only Son, we do not refuse even to undergo death. We are not so foolish and perverse as you, that we would rather throw off what saves and take up what kills. We do not run from the protection of heavenly medicine. We can see that a physician may cut with the knife, burn with the cautery, and bring the sick man to every kind of pain with burning mustard, and yet being cut, burned, eaten away and stung is not his enemy. It is good precisely because it takes away useless pains by means of pains applied for the sake of health. God wills that we dissolve death by death, dispel eternal torments by temporary ones, and cancel future, everlasting punishments by means of your punishments. For we are confident that when you take life from us, more can be given to us: eternal life in place of temporary life, incorruptible and everlasting life in place of frail and perishable life. You think it not enough that those who confess themselves Christians should merely be put to the sword, unless you inflict every kind of punishment on their bodies. It makes no difference what kind of death you choose to punish us with, so long as by it we are admitted to the enjoyment of eternal life, so long as by it your rage is put to death and we, on the contrary, are brought to life. If you think it wretched that I would rather be killed by any cruel punishment at all for the Son of God, then, to say nothing of the eternal glory of the blessed martyrs, I know that I must die by some kind of death or other. In short, I can show you many who die more cruelly in their beds, swollen by some internal abscess, or drawn up by the pain of sinews straining against themselves. What matters is the cause for which I hang, not the stake I hang from.

What do you say, most foolish king? Am I sent by you to these tortures, to a punishment of this kind, unjustly or justly? If unjustly, the cross will belong to you who nail me to it, not to me whom you have nailed; if justly, it is the guilt of my crime that will begin to torment me, not your punishment. Besides, as far as the outcome is concerned, it makes no difference whether I die at your hands by nail or by lance, with my hands bound behind my back or stretched out and spread wide, whether face down, bent over, or upright and raised high. It matters nothing whether you kill me as I rest in my bed, or cut through my neck with a sword as I stand, or take off my head with an axe; whether you bind me to a stake or to a cross, roast me with fire or bury me alive in the earth, hurl me from a rock or sink me in the sea; whether with a [?], straining with all your might, you strike my head far from me with one enormous blow, or with every refinement you sport with my body, piercing it slowly with ever finer arrows. Though your cruelty devise a hundred thousand forms of punishment, out of all of them only immortality will come to me through this death you inflict. I cannot but rejoice when you heap such things upon me, since I know that through these punishments every punishment can be brought to an end. And those things too which are external, and which I think your savagery may bring about, I judge to be no concern of mine: whether birds or dogs tear my body and cling to it, whether wild beasts with those cruel eyes leap upon me while you look on, whether as I lie on the ground I am reduced to the very bones by claws and teeth, since after all this I am safe with God. For when you have consumed my body with such great forces of your bestial savagery, the Creator of all things will restore and repair it, and indeed raise it from corruption to eternal incorruptibility. But you, our most unjust persecutor, must know that a punishment without end is coming upon you; and do not suppose that you will go unpunished, you who have decreed that the name of the only Son of God be put beneath your feet and trampled impiously and wickedly. It is the voice of the blessed apostle: The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is to come. That glory we shall surely possess if we choose to be killed by you rather than deny the Son of God. When that revelation and splendour shines upon all of us who believe, his servants will be blessed forever, set in his kingdom; you, on the other hand, if you resolve to persist in your faithlessness, will be in the outer darkness, as a deserter from his army and an assailant of the truth, one who has done the will of the devil. Hence, unless you pull yourself free of his snares, you must be tormented with him in unquenchable fire, as it is written. We say none of this of ourselves; for concerning you transgressors, concerning you blasphemers who deny that the only Son of God is his true Son, and concerning all who refuse to believe in him, we read what is set down in the most holy prophet: Their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched. If you remain in this madness, you will be forever in inescapable darkness. For just as we who confess the Son of God shall obtain the rewards of immortality and enjoy everlasting light, so you, who deny him, must be carried down to the setting of the sun and to eternal darkness. You will be led along the road you are keeping to, not to heaven, as the Arians falsely tell you, but to the hated stronghold of the world, to the left-hand path of the wicked and to impious Tartarus. For that road belongs to the renegade whose every wish you, his henchman, are found to carry out; it belongs, I say, to that serpent who turned you from the heavenly road to keep to this road of injustice. This is the broad and spacious way of which the Lord speaks in the Gospel, saying: How broad and spacious is the way that leads to destruction! If, then, you will not take thought for yourself, there can be no doubt that you are among those whom blessed John strikes when he says: Even now the axe is laid to the root of the trees; whoever does not bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire. You, then, and all who share with you, since you are most bitter trees bearing the fruits of death, sinning as you do against God, will be cut down unless you cross over to the heavenly road, and you will be hurled headlong, quicker than it takes to say it, into the deep abyss. From there you will doubtless see those whom you now unjustly persecute, as the rich man once saw Lazarus in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the friends of God, and of all the prophets, apostles and martyrs. You will not escape those punishments, Constantius, unless, first of all, you believe that the only Son of God is the true Son of God; and then, as has often been said, unless you confess that he has always reigned with the Father and reigns still, that is, without beginning or end, and move from the abominable assembly of the Arians to the catholic Church, that is, from death to life, and confess, as we catholics confess, that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are a perfect Trinity and have one Godhead.

So you hate Christians and persecute them in every way, as though your malice could overcome those who have set out on a hard and rough road. Though you scorn, deride and hate them, they are nonetheless willing throughout this present life to be poor, humble, obscure and exposed to your injuries, believing that by bearing for God's sake everything known to be bitter they will come to those surpassing rewards which the apostle says are to be gained: what no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered the heart of man, what the Lord has prepared for those who love him. Therefore, since God will bestow these things on those who love him, we who love God are confident that when we displease you, when we are punished by you, we please God. For your deadly sentence can have no power to punish us eternally, since you who condemn are yourself to be condemned, and indeed condemned to pay everlasting penalties. But we whom you torture, mangle and kill will be received into eternal joys; vast and immeasurable happiness will possess us, and everlasting blessedness will welcome us. Know, then, that it is rather to us that power has been given by God, so that while you think you are condemning us, we condemn you; while you presume you can punish us, we punish you, Constantius the sacrilegious. For he whom you deny deigned to give us, his bishops, authority, so that whatever we bind on earth is bound also in heaven. We endure temporal evils for God's sake so that we may obtain eternal goods. We flee the temporal things you offer us as goods, because eternal evils follow those goods of yours. That is why we have chosen to endure present things that you think harmful to us, so that, while our glorious confession endures in us, we may be found worthy to obtain eternal and immortal goods; just as you, together with those who, fearing you, are found to have obeyed your will and abandoned the commandments of God, because they chose present goods and despised future ones, will fall into immortal evils. For they are more to be desired than gold and much precious stone, and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb; for your servant keeps them, and in keeping them there is great reward. We know that this life which you labour so hard to take from us is very short; we know that both the goods and the evils of this life are brief, but that the goods of that eternal life which we long to obtain are everlasting. For we know that in place of these brief goods which you delight in and enjoy, eternal evils will follow for you; and that for us Christians, whom you despise and never cease to mangle with all the forces of your empire, eternal goods will follow in place of these brief evils. You have read that this is so in Psalm 125: The Lord has done great things for them; and further on: Those who sow in tears will reap in joy. Going, they went and wept, casting their seed; but coming, they will come with rejoicing, carrying their sheaves. And in Psalm 128: Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in his ways. You shall eat the labours of your fruits; blessed are you, and it shall be well with you. It will surely be well forever with those who have not denied the Son of God, who will enjoy the fruit of the labour of their holy confession; but for you, if you resolve to remain forever in the madness in which you now live, it will be ill everlastingly, and you will receive what Judas Iscariot now receives. Then we shall see you as a suppliant, and yet all the lamentation of your repentance will be of no avail, since it is here that either everlasting life or death is won. We want you to know that we are always turning these things over in our hearts and thinking on them day and night: your everlasting punishments and the eternal rewards and merits of God's servants; what he threatens as punishment to you, who deny him and persecute his name, and what, on the contrary, he promises as everlasting glory to those who confess him.
